{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZiAK8A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDI2xg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 61, "title": "Correct WD2793 FORCE INTERRUPT status and interrupt latching", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `183d1b79e0bdd6e1c718faf7653b740ea5a38fd7`, `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs:244` clears IRQ on every Status read. FORCE INTERRUPT at lines 345–350 calls `finish(0)`, discarding stored errors and retaining the previous status classification. D8 therefore loses its interrupt latch, while idle FORCE INTERRUPT after a sector command fails to select Type-I status. READY-transition handling also misses media changes made through mount/eject.

These discrepancies affect controller recovery and multi-record termination through both interfaces. No particular commercial-game failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Implement coherent Type-IV cancellation, status selection and interrupt acknowledgement through the existing Weave and Philips wiring. Preserve completed movement and sectors, device-clocked transfers, private-media ownership and cancellation safety.

## Context

Clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. [Issue #59](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/59) and [PR #60](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/60) explicitly deferred this correction.

Inspected technical references:

- [TI second-source TMS279X/WD279X manufacturer transcription](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pages 26 and 29: conditional interrupts, immediate-interrupt acknowledgement and busy-versus-idle status handling. This is an edited transcription without physical WD2793 confirmation.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc), `peekIRQ`, `getStatusReg`, `setCommandReg` and `startType4Cmd`: separate immediate latch, D0 release and DRQ cancellation. Its READY-condition handling is incomplete, and its status decoding must not override the manufacturer distinction.

Existing native tests and `tests/fixtures/philips.py` contain D8 expectations that incorrectly accept Status acknowledgement. Update these alongside the controller. PR #60 and `docs/validation.md` report 242 Rust and 146 browser passes and completed self-review; inspected CI steps now show successful native/browser checks. Submitted GitHub reviews are empty. Existing passes do not establish the new behavior. Planning executed no builds or tests.

Scope is Type-IV behavior within the existing instruction-boundary scheduler. Exact internal cancellation latency, too-rapid command replacement, full HLD lifecycle and additional FDC commands remain separate gaps. Retained WD scan/handbook failures and this turn's unavailable alternative references do not prevent this task.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Distinguish busy interruption from idle FORCE INTERRUPT. Busy interruption clears BUSY while retaining the interrupted status interpretation and stored errors, including LOST DATA. Idle execution selects Type-I status and refreshes supported live signals. Separate stored status from live READY/DRQ recomputation; document that distinction.
- [ ] Represent immediate IRQ separately from ordinary pending IRQ. D8 remains asserted across repeated Status reads, signal reads, elapsed time and ordinary commands; other nonzero Type-IV masks cannot release it. D0 disarms it and restores ordinary acknowledgement. Explicitly adopt the pinned upstream's command-boundary D0 release policy; the precise electrical release edge remains unmeasured. Test D8→Status, D8→ordinary command, D8→D0→Status and D8→D0→ordinary command. Reset clears both sources and masks.
- [ ] Support D1/D2 READY edges and D4 recurring index events, including combined masks. Acknowledgement must allow a later qualifying event to interrupt again without retriggering from an unchanged level. Include existing drive/motor controls and media insertion/ejection; preserve their separately documented lifecycle notifications. Ordinary accepted commands and D0 cancel conditional arming. Absent/stopped media produces no index events.
- [ ] Cancel pending movement, settling, searches, transfers and tails; deassert DRQ without unintended completion IRQ. Retain issued steps and completed sectors, discard staged incomplete writes, and prevent canceled events from resurrecting. Preserve write protection, dirty-media guards and exact exports.
- [ ] Add independent native sequence/status expectations in the disk suites. Cover busy Type-I/II versus idle status, overrun before cancellation, normal IRQ acknowledgement, immediate-latch sequences, conditional-mask combinations, repeated events, reset and cancellation phases. Check index boundaries with large, irregular and single-cycle ticks. Record meaningful baseline failures and corrected results; do not derive expectations from production helpers.
- [ ] Extend original CPU diagnostics through both interfaces on MSX1/MSX2 and both raw geometries. Assert observable status/signal traces and complete exported images. Run compiled-Wasm coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Keep FDC IRQ disconnected from CPU IRQ, preserve slot isolation, firmware/sub-ROM/mapper coexistence, SRAM, PSG/SCC/SCC-I audio, browser lifecycle and provenance. No proprietary inputs or BIOS bypasses are required.
- [ ] Update affected documentation and obsolete fixture expectations. The Coordinator runs and reports README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare original register traces with pinned upstream, excluding its documented conditional/status limitations. Additional checks may use already lawfully available software. These comparisons were not performed during planning; diagnostic success does not establish commercial-game compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
